title.zh: 卷一百四十九 列傳第三十七 蹇義 夏原吉
title.en: Volume 149 Biographies 37: Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji
title.raw: 卷一百四十九 列傳第三十七 蹇義 夏原吉 Volume 149 Biographies 37: Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji

sentences.zh: 蹇義夏原吉

translations.literal: Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji

sentences.zh: 〈（俞士吉李文郁鄒師顏）〉

translations.literal: (Yu Shiji, Li Wenyu, Zou Shiyan)
translations.idiomatic: (Yu Shiji, Li Wenyu, Zou Shiyan)

sentences.zh: 蹇義，字宜之，巴人，初名容。洪武十八年進士。授中書舍人，奏事稱旨。帝問：「汝蹇叔後乎？」容頓首不敢對。帝嘉其誠篤，為更名義，手書賜之。滿三載當遷，特命滿九載，曰：「朕且用義。」由是朝夕侍左右，小心敬慎，未嘗忤色。惠帝既即位，推太祖意，超擢吏部右侍郎。是時齊泰、黃子澄當國，外興大師，內改制度，義無所建明。國子博士王紳遺書責之，義不能答。

translations.literal: Jian Yi, style Yizhi, was a man of Ba and was originally named Rong. In Hongwu year eighteen he became a jinshi. He was appointed Secretariat Drafter, and his memorials suited the emperor's intent. The emperor asked, "Are you a descendant of Jian Shu?" Rong kowtowed and did not dare answer. The emperor praised his sincerity and simplicity, changed his name to Yi, and bestowed it on him in his own handwriting. When Yi had completed three years and should have been promoted, the emperor specifically ordered him to complete nine years, saying, "I am about to use Yi." From then on Yi attended at the emperor's side morning and evening, careful and reverent, and never offended his expression. When Emperor Hui came to the throne, he inferred Taizu's intent and exceptionally promoted Yi to right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel. At this time Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng controlled the government, raising great armies abroad and changing institutions at home, but Yi made no proposals or clarifications. Wang Shen, a doctor of the Directorate of Education, sent him a letter reproaching him, and Yi could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi, style Yizhi, was from Ba and was originally named Rong. He became a jinshi in Hongwu 18 and was appointed Secretariat Drafter, where his memorials pleased the emperor. The emperor asked, "Are you a descendant of Jian Shu?" Rong kowtowed and did not dare reply. Admiring his sincerity, the emperor changed his name to Yi and bestowed the written name in his own hand. After Yi had completed three years and was due for promotion, the emperor specifically ordered him to serve the full nine years, saying, "I am about to make use of Yi." From then on Yi attended the emperor morning and evening, cautious and reverent, never offending him. When Emperor Hui came to the throne, he inferred Taizu's intention and exceptionally promoted Yi to right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel. At that time Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng controlled the government, raising major armies outside and altering institutions within, but Yi offered no constructive proposals. Wang Shen, a doctor of the Directorate of Education, sent him a letter of reproach, and Yi could not answer.

sentences.zh: 燕師入，迎附，遷左侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Yan army entered, he welcomed and submitted; he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan's army entered the capital, he welcomed them and submitted; he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 數月，進尚書。

translations.literal: Several months later, he was advanced to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時方務反建文之政，所更易者悉罷之。

translations.literal: At that time the court was bent on reversing the Jianwen policies, and all that had been changed was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then intent on undoing the policies of the Jianwen reign, and every measure that had been altered was rescinded.

sentences.zh: 義從容言曰：「損益貴適時宜。

translations.literal: Yi said calmly, "In adding or subtracting, what matters is suiting the time.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi said calmly, "Whether to add or cut depends on what suits the times.

sentences.zh: 前改者固不當，今必欲盡復者，亦未悉當也。」

translations.literal: The earlier changes were indeed improper, yet to insist now on restoring everything is also not entirely right."
translations.idiomatic: The earlier reforms were indeed wrong, but to insist now on restoring everything wholesale is not entirely right either."

sentences.zh: 因舉數事陳說本末。

translations.literal: He thereupon cited several cases and set forth their full course.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited several examples and explained each from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，從其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised this and followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle he also served as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongle reign he was also appointed Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 帝有所傳諭太子，輒遣義，能委曲導意。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor had instructions to convey to the Heir Apparent, he would send Yi, who could tactfully guide the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor wished to convey something to the Crown Prince, he would send Jian Yi, who could convey the intent tactfully and fully.

sentences.zh: 帝與太子俱愛重之。

translations.literal: Both the Emperor and the Heir Apparent cherished and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Emperor and the Crown Prince held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝巡北京，命輔皇太子監國。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Emperor toured Beijing and ordered him to assist the Heir Apparent in governing the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the Emperor toured Beijing, he was ordered to assist the Crown Prince in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 義熟典故，達治體，軍國事皆倚辦。

translations.literal: Yi was versed in precedent and understood the structure of governance; military and state affairs all relied on him to handle.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi was versed in precedent and understood how government worked; military and civil affairs alike were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 時舊臣見親用者，戶部尚書夏原吉與義齊名，中外稱曰「蹇、夏」。

translations.literal: Among old officials then in close use, Minister of Revenue Xia Yuanji was equally famed with Yi, and within and without the court they were called "Jian and Xia."
translations.idiomatic: Among the veteran officials then in favor, Minister of Revenue Xia Yuanji was as renowned as Jian Yi, and throughout the court and empire they were known as "Jian and Xia."

sentences.zh: 滿三考，帝親宴二人便殿，褒揚甚至。

translations.literal: When three terms of evaluation were complete, the Emperor personally feasted the two men in the side hall and praised them to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When they had completed three rounds of performance review, the Emperor personally entertained them in a side hall and lavished praise upon them.

sentences.zh: 數奉命兼理他部事，職務填委，處之裕如。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly ordered on commission to handle other ministries' affairs; duties piled up, yet he dealt with them at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly ordered to handle affairs of other ministries on commission; though duties piled up, he managed them with ease.

sentences.zh: 十七年以父喪歸，帝及太子皆遣官賜祭。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he returned home on his father's death; both the Emperor and the Heir Apparent sent officials with offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he went home to mourn his father; both the Emperor and the Crown Prince sent officials with sacrificial gifts.

sentences.zh: 詔起復。

translations.literal: An edict recalled him to office before mourning was finished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him recalled to office before the mourning period had ended.

sentences.zh: 十九年，三殿災，敕廷臣二十六人巡行天下。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Three Halls burned; the Emperor ordered twenty-six court officials to tour the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, when fire destroyed the Three Halls, the Emperor ordered twenty-six court officials to tour the empire.

sentences.zh: 義及給事中馬俊分巡應天諸府，問軍民疾苦，黜文武長吏擾民者數人，條興革數十事奏行之。

translations.literal: Yi and Supervising Secretary Ma Jun separately toured the prefectures of Yingtian, inquired into the hardships of soldiers and civilians, dismissed several civil and military chiefs who harassed the people, and memorialized dozens of items to institute or abolish, which were enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi and Supervising Secretary Ma Jun toured the prefectures of the Yingtian region, inquired into the hardships of soldiers and civilians, removed several civil and military officials who had harassed the people, and submitted dozens of proposals for reform, which were put into effect.

sentences.zh: 還治部事。

translations.literal: He returned to handle the affairs of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to manage the affairs of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝北征還，以太子曲宥呂震婿主事張鶴朝參失儀，罪義不匡正，逮義系錦衣衛獄。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Emperor returned from the northern campaign, because the Heir Apparent had unduly pardoned Lü Zhen's son-in-law, Director Zhang He, for impropriety at court audience, Yi was blamed for not correcting this and was seized and imprisoned in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the Emperor returned from the northern campaign, he blamed Jian Yi for failing to correct the Crown Prince, who had unduly excused Director Zhang He—Lü Zhen's son-in-law—for a breach of court etiquette at audience; Jian Yi was arrested and imprisoned in the Embroidered Uniform Guard jail.

sentences.zh: 又明年春得釋。

translations.literal: The spring of the year after next he was released.
translations.idiomatic: He was released the following spring.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，義、原吉皆以元老為中外所信。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, Yi and Yuanji were both trusted within and without as senior veterans.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor ascended the throne, Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji were both trusted throughout the court and empire as senior statesmen.

sentences.zh: 帝又念義監國時舊勞，尤厚倚之。

translations.literal: The Emperor also recalled Yi's old labors when governing the realm and relied on him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also remembered Jian Yi's service when the Crown Prince had governed the realm, and relied on him all the more heavily.

sentences.zh: 首進義少保，賜冠服、象笏、玉帶，兼食二祿。

translations.literal: He first advanced Yi to Junior Guardian, bestowed cap and robe, ivory tablet, and jade belt, and granted double stipends.
translations.idiomatic: He first promoted Jian Yi to Junior Guardian, bestowed court dress, an ivory tablet, and a jade belt, and granted him double stipends.

sentences.zh: 歷進少師，賜銀章一，文曰「繩愆糾繆」。

translations.literal: He was advanced in turn to Junior Preceptor and given one silver seal inscribed "Correcting faults and remedying errors."
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Junior Preceptor and given a silver seal inscribed "Correcting faults and remedying errors."

sentences.zh: 已，復賜璽書曰：「曩朕監國，卿以先朝舊臣，日侍左右。

translations.literal: Soon after, he again bestowed an imperial letter saying: "Formerly when I governed the realm, you as an old minister of the previous reign attended me daily.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he bestowed another imperial letter, which read: "When I was governing the realm as heir, you, as a veteran of the previous reign, attended me day after day.

sentences.zh: 兩京肇建，政務方殷，卿勞心焦思，不恤身家，二十余年，夷險一節。

translations.literal: As the two capitals were first established and state affairs were pressing, you toiled in mind and burned with thought, heedless of self and family—for more than twenty years one integrity through ease and peril.
translations.idiomatic: As the two capitals were being built and government affairs pressed hard upon us, you labored with anxious devotion, heedless of yourself and your family—for more than twenty years you held the same integrity through good times and bad.

sentences.zh: 朕承大統，贊襄治理，不懈益恭。

translations.literal: When I received the great succession, you assisted in governance, never slackening but growing more respectful.
translations.idiomatic: When I inherited the throne, you assisted in governing the realm, never slackening but growing ever more devoted.

sentences.zh: 朕篤念不忘，茲以已意，創制『蹇忠貞印』賜卿。

translations.literal: I cherish this and do not forget; now of my own accord I have created the "Jian Loyal and Upright Seal" to bestow on you.
translations.idiomatic: I hold this in deep remembrance; of my own accord I have had made the "Seal of Jian the Loyal and Upright" and bestow it upon you.

sentences.zh: 俾藏於家，傳之後世，知朕君臣共濟艱難，相與有成也。」

translations.literal: Keep it in your house and pass it to later generations, so they may know how ruler and minister together crossed hardship and achieved success."
translations.idiomatic: Keep it in your household and pass it down to posterity, so they may know how we, ruler and minister, weathered hardship together and achieved what we did."

sentences.zh: 時惟楊士奇亦得賜「貞一」印及敕。

translations.literal: At that time only Yang Shiqi also received the "Upright and One" seal and an edict.
translations.idiomatic: At that time only Yang Shiqi likewise received the "Upright and One" seal and an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 尋命與英國公輔及原吉同監修《太宗實錄》。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered, together with the Duke of Ying, Fu, and Yuanji, to supervise compilation of the Veritable Records of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered, together with the Duke of Ying, Zhang Fu, and Xia Yuanji, to supervise compilation of the Veritable Records of the Taizong Emperor.

sentences.zh: 義視原吉尤重厚，然過於周慎。

translations.literal: Yi regarded Yuanji as especially weighty and generous, yet he himself was overly thorough and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi regarded Xia Yuanji with especial respect and warmth, yet he himself was excessively thorough and cautious.

sentences.zh: 士奇嘗於帝前謂義曰：「何過慮？」

translations.literal: Shiqi once said to Yi before the Emperor, "Why worry so much?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi once said to Jian Yi in the Emperor's presence, "Why such excessive worry?"

sentences.zh: 義曰：「恐鹵莽為後憂耳。」

translations.literal: Yi said, "I fear rashness will bring trouble later."
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi replied, "I fear that acting rashly will bring trouble later."

sentences.zh: 帝兩是之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved both.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved of both views.

sentences.zh: 楊榮嘗毀義。

translations.literal: Yang Rong once slandered Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong once spoke ill of Jian Yi.

sentences.zh: 帝不直榮。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not side with Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not take Rong's side.

sentences.zh: 義頓首言：「榮無他。

translations.literal: Yi kowtowed and said, "Rong has no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi kowtowed and said, "Rong means no harm.

sentences.zh: 即左右有讒榮者，願陛下慎察。」

translations.literal: If those at your side slander Rong, I beg Your Majesty to examine carefully."
translations.idiomatic: If anyone at your side speaks against him, I beg Your Majesty to look into it carefully."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「吾固弗信也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said, "I never believed it in the first place."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor smiled and said, "I never believed it in the first place."

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，委寄益重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, his trust in Yi grew heavier still.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuanzong Emperor ascended the throne, his reliance on Jian Yi grew even greater.

sentences.zh: 時方修獻陵，帝欲遵遺詔從儉約，以問義、原吉。

translations.literal: At that time the Xian Mausoleum was under construction; the Emperor wished to follow the testament and keep to frugality, and asked Yi and Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: The Xian Mausoleum was then under construction; the Emperor wished to follow his father's testament and keep the work frugal, and consulted Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 二人力贊曰：「聖見高遠，出於至孝，萬世之利也。」

translations.literal: The two men strongly praised, saying, "Your sage vision is far-reaching, springing from utmost filial piety—a benefit for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Both men strongly endorsed the plan, saying, "Your sage vision is far-reaching and springs from deepest filial piety; it will benefit generations to come."

sentences.zh: 帝親為規畫，三月而陵成，宏麗不及長陵，其後諸帝因以為制。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally planned it; in three months the mausoleum was complete—its grandeur did not match the Chang Mausoleum, and later emperors took this as the model.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally oversaw the design; the mausoleum was completed in three months. It was less grand than the Chang Mausoleum, and later emperors took this as their standard.

sentences.zh: 迨世宗營永陵，始益崇侈雲。

translations.literal: Only when Emperor Shizong built the Yong Mausoleum did extravagance grow greater.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the Shizong Emperor built the Yong Mausoleum did imperial tombs grow more lavish.

sentences.zh: 帝征樂安，義、原吉及諸學士皆從，預軍中機務，賜鞍馬甲胄弓劍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Le'an, Yi, Yuanji, and the academicians all followed, taking part in military counsels, and were given saddles, horses, armor, bows, and swords.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor campaigned against Le'an, Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji, and the Hanlin academicians all accompanied him, took part in military planning, and were given saddles, horses, armor, bows, and swords.

sentences.zh: 及還，賚予甚厚。

translations.literal: On return, rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, the rewards were very generous.

sentences.zh: 三年從巡邊還。

translations.literal: In the third year he returned from accompanying the border tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the reign he returned from accompanying the border inspection tour.

sentences.zh: 帝以義、原吉、士奇、榮四人者皆已老，賜璽書曰：「卿等皆祖宗遺老，畀輔朕躬。

translations.literal: The Emperor, seeing that Yi, Yuanji, Shiqi, and Rong were all old, bestowed an imperial letter: "You are all surviving elders left by our ancestors, entrusted to assist my person.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji, Yang Shiqi, and Yang Rong were all advanced in years, the Emperor bestowed an imperial letter: "You are all surviving elders left by our ancestors, entrusted to assist me.

sentences.zh: 今黃髮危齒，不宜復典冗劇，傷朝廷優老待賢之禮。

translations.literal: Now with yellow hair and failing teeth, you should not again preside over tedious duties, harming the court's rite of honoring age and treating the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Now that your hair has turned white and your teeth are failing, you should no longer bear the burden of heavy routine duties, to the detriment of the court's policy of honoring the aged and treating the worthy with care.

sentences.zh: 可輟所務，朝夕在朕左右討論至理，共寧邦家。

translations.literal: You may set aside your duties and morning and evening be at my side to discuss ultimate principles and together bring peace to the state and family.
translations.idiomatic: You may set aside your official duties and remain at my side day and night to discuss fundamental principles and together bring peace to the realm.

sentences.zh: 官祿悉如舊。」

translations.literal: Rank and stipend shall all remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: Your rank and stipends shall all remain unchanged."

sentences.zh: 明年，郭琎代為尚書。

translations.literal: The next year Guo Jin replaced him as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Guo Jin replaced him as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋以胡濙言，命義等四人議天下官吏軍民建言章奏。

translations.literal: Soon, on Hu Ying's recommendation, the Emperor ordered Yi and the other four to deliberate on memorials from officials, soldiers, and civilians throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on Hu Ying's recommendation, the Emperor ordered Jian Yi and the other three to deliberate on memorials submitted by officials, soldiers, and civilians throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 復賜義銀章，文曰「忠厚寬宏」。

translations.literal: He again bestowed on Yi a silver seal inscribed "Loyal, generous, broad, and magnanimous."
translations.idiomatic: He again bestowed on Jian Yi a silver seal inscribed "Loyal, generous, broad, and magnanimous."

sentences.zh: 七年詔有司為義營新第於文明門內。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered the authorities to build Yi a new residence inside the Wenming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the reign an edict ordered the authorities to build Jian Yi a new residence inside the Wenming Gate.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，齋宿得疾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Yi fell ill while observing fast and vigil.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong Emperor ascended the throne, Jian Yi fell ill while observing ritual fasting and vigil.

sentences.zh: 遣醫往視，問所欲言。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent physicians to see him and asked what he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent physicians to attend him and asked what he wished to say.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下初嗣大寶，望敬守祖宗成憲，始終不渝耳。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty has newly succeeded to the great mandate; I hope you will reverently keep the established statutes of the ancestors, never wavering from first to last."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your Majesty has only just inherited the throne; I hope you will reverently uphold the established institutions of your ancestors and never depart from them."

sentences.zh: 遂卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He then died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He then died, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚忠定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Settled.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Zhongding (Loyal and Settled).

sentences.zh: 義為人質直孝友，善處僚友間，未嘗一語傷物。

translations.literal: Yi as a man was plain, upright, filial, and friendly; he was skilled among colleagues and never once spoke to wound others.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi was by nature plainspoken, upright, filial, and friendly; he handled relations among colleagues well and never spoke a word that wounded anyone.

sentences.zh: 士奇常言：「張詠之不飾玩好，傅堯俞之遇人以誠，範景仁之不設城府，義兼有之。」

translations.literal: Shiqi often said, "Zhang Yong's not adorning himself with curios, Fu Yaoyu's treating people with sincerity, Fan Jingren's setting up no hidden schemes—Yi combined them all."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi often said, "Zhang Yong's disdain for ornamental luxuries, Fu Yaoyu's sincerity toward others, and Fan Jingren's freedom from hidden designs—Jian Yi combined them all."

sentences.zh: 子英，有詩名，以蔭為尚寶司丞，歷官太常少卿。

translations.literal: His son Ying was famed for poetry; by hereditary privilege he became Director of the Imperial Seals Office and rose to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying was renowned as a poet; through hereditary privilege he became a director in the Imperial Seals Office and eventually rose to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 夏原吉，字維喆，其先德興人。

translations.literal: Xia Yuanji, courtesy name Weizhe, his ancestors were men of Dexing.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji, courtesy name Weizhe, came from a family originally of Dexing.

sentences.zh: 父時敏，官湘陰教諭，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His father Shimin served as instructor of Xiangyin and there made his home.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shimin served as instructor in Xiangyin, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 原吉早孤，力學養母。

translations.literal: Yuanji was orphaned early; he studied hard and supported his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji lost his father early; he studied diligently and supported his mother.

sentences.zh: 以鄉薦入太學，選入禁中書制誥。

translations.literal: Recommended from the prefecture he entered the Imperial Academy and was chosen to draft edicts within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended through the provincial examination, he entered the Imperial Academy and was selected to draft imperial edicts within the palace.

sentences.zh: 諸生或喧笑，原吉危坐儼然。

translations.literal: When other students sometimes laughed and made noise, Yuanji sat upright with stern composure.
translations.idiomatic: While other students sometimes laughed and chatted noisily, Yuanji sat upright with stern composure.

sentences.zh: 太祖诇而異之。

translations.literal: Taizu observed this and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu noticed this and regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 曹務叢脞，處之悉有條理，尚書郁新甚重之。

translations.literal: Office business was tangled and piled; he handled it all with order, and Minister Yu Xin greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Though ministry business was tangled and piled high, he handled it all with order, and Minister Yu Xin held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 有劉郎中者，忌其能。

translations.literal: There was a Director Liu who envied his ability.
translations.idiomatic: A certain Director Liu envied his ability.

sentences.zh: 會新劾諸司怠事者。

translations.literal: When Xin impeached those in various offices who neglected their duties,
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Xin impeached officials in various offices for neglecting their duties,

sentences.zh: 帝欲宥之，新持不可。

translations.literal: the Emperor wished to pardon them, but Xin insisted it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor wished to pardon them, but Yu Xin insisted that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，問：「誰教若？」

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and asked, "Who taught you?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angry and asked, "Who told you to do this?"

sentences.zh: 新頓首曰：「堂後書算生。」

translations.literal: Xin kowtowed and said, "The clerks and calculators behind the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xin kowtowed and said, "The clerks and accountants behind the hall."

sentences.zh: 帝乃下書算生於獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent the clerks and calculators to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then had the clerks and accountants imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 劉郎中遂言：「教尚書者，原吉也。」

translations.literal: Director Liu then said, "The one who instructed the Minister is Yuanji."
translations.idiomatic: Director Liu then said, "The one who instructed the Minister was Yuanji."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「原吉能佐尚書理部事，汝欲陷之耶！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Yuanji can assist the Minister in handling the ministry's affairs—do you wish to entrap him!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Yuanji assists the Minister in running the ministry—are you trying to frame him?"

sentences.zh: 劉郎中與書算生皆棄市。

translations.literal: Director Liu and the clerks and calculators were all executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Director Liu and the clerks and accountants were all executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 建文初，擢戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年充采訪使。

translations.literal: The next year he served as investigation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed investigation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 巡福建，所過郡邑，核吏治，咨民隱。

translations.literal: He toured Fujian; in every prefecture and county he passed he examined officials' governance and inquired into the people's hidden hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He toured Fujian; in every prefecture and county he passed he examined how officials governed and inquired into the people's hidden grievances.

sentences.zh: 人皆悅服。

translations.literal: All were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone was pleased and submitted to his authority.

sentences.zh: 久之，移駐蘄州。

translations.literal: After a long while he moved his station to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he moved his headquarters to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，或執原吉以獻。

translations.literal: When Chengzu took the throne, some seized Yuanji to present him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chengzu Emperor took the throne, some seized Yuanji to present him as a captive.

sentences.zh: 帝釋之，轉左侍郎。

translations.literal: The Emperor released him and transferred him to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor released him and appointed him Left Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 或言原吉建文時用事，不可信。

translations.literal: Some said that during Jianwen Yuanji had held power and could not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that Yuanji had held power under the Jianwen Emperor and could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，與蹇義同進尚書。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen and advanced him together with Jian Yi to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not hear of it and promoted him to Minister of Revenue together with Jian Yi.

sentences.zh: 偕義等詳定賦役諸制。

translations.literal: Together with Yi and others he worked out in detail the regulations on taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Jian Yi and others he worked out in detail the regulations on taxes and corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 建白三十余事，皆簡便易遵守。

translations.literal: He proposed more than thirty items, all simple, convenient, and easy to observe.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed more than thirty measures, all simple, practical, and easy to enforce.

sentences.zh: 曰：「行之而難繼者，且重困民，吾不忍也。」

translations.literal: He said, "What is hard to continue once put in practice and moreover heavily burdens the people—I cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I cannot bear to impose measures that are hard to sustain once enacted and that would further burden the people."

sentences.zh: 浙西大水，有司治不效。

translations.literal: Western Zhejiang suffered great flood; the authorities' efforts were ineffective.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhejiang suffered severe flooding, and the local authorities' efforts proved ineffective.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，命原吉治之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle the Emperor ordered Yuanji to remedy it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongle reign the Emperor ordered Yuanji to take charge of relief efforts.

sentences.zh: 尋命侍郎李文郁為之副，復使僉都御史俞士吉賫水利書賜之。

translations.literal: Soon Vice Minister Li Wenyu was appointed his deputy, and Assistant Censor-in-Chief Yu Shiji was again sent bearing a book on water control as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given Vice Minister Li Wenyu as deputy, and Assistant Censor-in-Chief Yu Shiji was again dispatched with an imperial book on water control as a gift.

sentences.zh: 原吉請循禹三江入海故跡，浚吳淞下流，上接太湖，而度地為閘，以時蓄泄。

translations.literal: Yuanji requested to follow the old traces by which Yu's three rivers entered the sea, dredge the lower Wusong, connect upward to Tai Lake, and according to the terrain build sluices to store and release water in season.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji proposed following the ancient course by which Yu the Great's three rivers had reached the sea, dredging the lower Wusong River to connect with Lake Tai, and building sluices at suitable points to store and release water according to the season.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 役十余萬人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand men were put to labor.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand laborers were mobilized.

sentences.zh: 原吉布衣徒步，日夜經畫。

translations.literal: Yuanji wore plain cloth and went on foot, planning day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji wore plain clothes and went on foot, planning the work day and night.

sentences.zh: 盛暑不張蓋，曰：「民勞，吾何忍獨適。」

translations.literal: In the height of summer he would not raise a canopy, saying, "The people labor—how can I bear to enjoy comfort alone?"
translations.idiomatic: In the height of summer he would not raise a parasol, saying, "The people are laboring—how can I bear to enjoy comfort alone?"

sentences.zh: 事竣，還京師，言水雖由故道入海，而支流未盡疏泄，非經久計。

translations.literal: When the work was done he returned to the capital and said that though the water now entered the sea by the old channel, tributaries were not fully dredged and drained—this was no lasting plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished he returned to the capital and reported that although water now reached the sea by the old channel, tributary streams had not been fully dredged—a solution that would not last.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，原吉復行，浚白茆塘、劉家河、大黃浦。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Yuanji went out again and dredged Baimao Pond, the Liu Family River, and the Great Huangpu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Yuanji set out again and dredged Baimao Pond, the Liu Family River, and the Great Huangpu.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿袁復為之副。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Fu served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Fu, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 已，復命陜西參政宋性佐之。

translations.literal: Soon after, Administrative Commissioner Song Xing of Shaanxi was ordered to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Administrative Commissioner Song Xing of Shaanxi was ordered to assist him.

sentences.zh: 九月工畢，水泄，蘇、松農田大利。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the work was finished, the water drained, and the fields of Suzhou and Songjiang greatly benefited.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the work was completed, the water drained away, and agriculture in Suzhou and Songjiang benefited greatly.

sentences.zh: 三年還。

translations.literal: In the third year he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 其夏，浙西大饑。

translations.literal: That summer western Zhejiang suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: That summer western Zhejiang suffered severe famine.

sentences.zh: 命原吉率俞士吉、袁復及左通政趙居任往振，發粟三十萬石，給牛種。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Yuanji to lead Yu Shiji, Yuan Fu, and Left Commissioner Zhao Juren to give relief, issuing three hundred thousand piculs of grain and supplying oxen and seed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Yuanji to lead Yu Shiji, Yuan Fu, and Left Commissioner Zhao Juren to provide relief, distributing three hundred thousand piculs of grain and supplying oxen and seed.

sentences.zh: 有請召民佃水退淤田益賦者，原吉馳疏止之。

translations.literal: Some requested that the people be summoned to till silt fields left when the water receded and increase the tax levy; Yuanji sent a hurried memorial to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed summoning people to farm silted fields left by the receding flood and increasing the tax levy, Yuanji sent an urgent memorial to halt the plan.

sentences.zh: 姚廣孝還自浙西，稱原吉曰：「古之遺愛也。」

translations.literal: Yao Guangxiao returned from western Zhejiang and praised Yuanji, saying, "A love left behind like those of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Guangxiao returned from western Zhejiang, he praised Yuanji, saying, "He has the enduring benevolence of the ancients."

sentences.zh: 亡何，郁新卒，召還，理部事。

translations.literal: Before long Yu Xin died; Yuanji was recalled to handle the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu Xin died; Yuanji was recalled to manage affairs at the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 首請裁冗食，平賦役；

translations.literal: He first requested to cut redundant consumption and level taxes and corvée;
translations.idiomatic: His first proposals were to cut redundant government spending and equalize taxes and corvée labor;

sentences.zh: 嚴鹽法、錢鈔之禁；

translations.literal: to tighten prohibitions on the salt laws and paper money;
translations.idiomatic: to enforce the salt monopoly and restrictions on paper currency;

sentences.zh: 清倉場，廣屯種，以給邊蘇民，且便商賈。

translations.literal: to clear the granaries, expand military colonies, thereby supplying the frontier and relieving the people, and also facilitating merchants.
translations.idiomatic: to clear the granaries, expand military farming colonies to supply the frontier and relieve the people, and facilitate commerce.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 凡中外戶口、府庫、田賦贏縮之數，各以小簡書置懷中，時檢閱之。

translations.literal: For all figures within and without on households, treasuries, and gains and losses in land tax, he kept each on a small slip in his bosom and reviewed them from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: He kept slips in his pocket recording figures for households, treasuries, and land-tax surpluses and deficits throughout the empire, and reviewed them regularly.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝問：「天下錢、谷幾何？」

translations.literal: One day the Emperor asked, "How much are the realm's money and grain?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the Emperor asked, "How much money and grain does the empire hold?"

sentences.zh: 對甚悉，以是益重之。

translations.literal: He answered very fully, and for this the Emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He answered in full detail, and the Emperor valued him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 當是時，兵革初定，論「靖難」功臣封賞，分封諸藩，增設武衛百司。

translations.literal: At that time, with warfare only just settled, the court debated rewards and enfeoffments for meritorious ministers of the "Pacification of Difficulties," enfeoffed the various princes, and newly established the hundred offices of military guards.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, with warfare only just ended, the court debated rewards for meritorious ministers of the "Pacification of Difficulties," enfeoffed the imperial princes, and expanded the military guards and government offices.

sentences.zh: 已，又發卒八十萬問罪安南、中官造巨艦通海外諸國、大起北都宮闕。

translations.literal: Then eight hundred thousand troops were again sent to punish Annam, eunuchs built great ships to reach overseas states, and the palaces of the northern capital were raised on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: Then eight hundred thousand troops were sent to punish Annam, eunuchs built great ships to reach overseas countries, and construction of the northern capital's palaces was undertaken on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 供億轉輸以鉅萬萬計，皆取給戶曹。

translations.literal: Supplies and transport ran to tens of billions, all drawn from the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies and transport costs ran into the tens of billions, all drawn from the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 原吉悉心計應之，國用不絀。

translations.literal: Yuanji with full care calculated to meet it, and state expenditure did not fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji calculated carefully to meet every demand, and state finances never ran short.

sentences.zh: 六年命督軍民輸材北都，詔以錦衣官校從，治怠事者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to supervise soldiers and civilians transporting materials to the northern capital; an edict sent Embroidered Uniform Guard officers to accompany him and punish those who neglected their duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was ordered to supervise the transport of building materials to the northern capital; an edict sent Embroidered Uniform Guard officers to accompany him and punish negligence.

sentences.zh: 原吉慮犯者眾，告戒而後行，人皆感悅。

translations.literal: Yuanji feared many would offend; he gave warnings before setting out, and all were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that many would be punished, Yuanji issued warnings before setting out, and everyone was grateful.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝北巡，命兼攝行在禮部、兵部、都察院事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the Emperor toured the north, he was ordered concurrently to handle the traveling capital's Ministry of Rites, Ministry of War, and Censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the Emperor toured the north, Yuanji was ordered concurrently to handle affairs of the traveling capital's Ministries of Rites and War and the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 有二指揮冒月廩，帝欲斬之。

translations.literal: Two commanders had falsely claimed monthly rations; the Emperor wished to behead them.
translations.idiomatic: Two commanders had fraudulently claimed monthly rations; the Emperor wished to execute them.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「非律也，假實為盜，將何以加？」

translations.literal: Yuanji said, "This is not according to law. If one falsely claims goods as theft, how can punishment be increased?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji said, "This is not according to law. If false claims are treated as theft, what further penalty could be applied?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then relented.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝北征，輔太孫留守北京，總行在九卿事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the Emperor campaigned north, he assisted the Imperial Grandson in remaining at Beijing and oversaw all traveling-capital ministerial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the Emperor campaigned north, he assisted the imperial grandson in governing Beijing and oversaw all ministerial affairs at the traveling capital.

sentences.zh: 時諸司草創，每旦，原吉入佐太孫參決庶務。

translations.literal: At that time the various offices were newly established; each morning Yuanji entered to assist the Imperial Grandson in deciding routine affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the various offices were still being established; each morning Yuanji entered to assist the imperial grandson in deciding routine affairs.

sentences.zh: 朝退，諸曹郎御史環請事。

translations.literal: After court, bureau directors, secretaries, and censors surrounded him seeking decisions.
translations.idiomatic: After court, bureau directors, secretaries, and censors surrounded him seeking decisions on pending matters.

sentences.zh: 原吉口答手書，不動聲色。

translations.literal: Yuanji answered by mouth and wrote by hand, without change of voice or countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji answered orally while writing by hand, without a change in voice or expression.

sentences.zh: 北達行在，南啟監國，京師肅然。

translations.literal: Northward he reached the traveling court; southward he reported to the regency—the capital was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He reported north to the traveling court and south to the regency in Nanjing, and the capital was orderly throughout.

sentences.zh: 帝還，賜鈔幣、鞍馬、牢醴，慰勞有加。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned, he bestowed paper money, saddles and horses, and provisions, with extra consolation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor returned, he bestowed paper money, saddles and horses, and provisions, with special words of consolation and reward.

sentences.zh: 尋從還南京，命侍太孫周行鄉落，觀民間疾苦。

translations.literal: Soon he accompanied the return to Nanjing and was ordered to attend the Imperial Grandson on tours through villages to observe the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He soon accompanied the court back to Nanjing and was ordered to attend the imperial grandson on tours through villages to observe the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 原吉取齏黍以進，曰：「願殿下食此，知民艱。」

translations.literal: Yuanji took pickled grain and presented it, saying, "I hope Your Highness will eat this and know the people's hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji brought forward pickled grain and presented it, saying, "I hope Your Highness will eat this and understand the people's hardship."

sentences.zh: 九載滿，與蹇義皆宴便殿，帝指二人謂群臣曰：「高皇帝養賢以貽朕。

translations.literal: When nine years were complete, he and Jian Yi were both feasted in the side hall; the Emperor pointed to the two and told the ministers, "The High Emperor nurtured the worthy to bequeath to me.
translations.idiomatic: When nine years of service were complete, he and Jian Yi were both feasted in a side hall; the Emperor pointed to them and told the ministers, "The Hongwu Emperor nurtured worthy men to bequeath to me.

sentences.zh: 欲觀古名臣，此其人矣。」

translations.literal: If one wishes to see famous ministers of old, these are the men."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to see the famous ministers of antiquity, here they are."

sentences.zh: 自是屢侍太孫，往來兩京，在道隨事納忠，多所裨益。

translations.literal: From then on he repeatedly attended the Imperial Grandson, traveling between the two capitals; on the road he offered loyal counsel as occasions arose, with much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he often attended the imperial grandson, traveling between the two capitals and offering loyal counsel along the way to great effect.

sentences.zh: 十八年，北京宮室成，使原吉南召太子、太孫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the Beijing palaces were complete, Yuanji was sent south to summon the Heir Apparent and Imperial Grandson.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, when the Beijing palaces were completed, Yuanji was sent south to summon the Crown Prince and imperial grandson.

sentences.zh: 既還，原吉言：「連歲營建，今告成。

translations.literal: After returning, Yuanji said, "Construction has continued for successive years; now it is announced complete.
translations.idiomatic: After returning, Yuanji said, "Construction has continued for years; now it is finished.

sentences.zh: 宜撫流亡，蠲逋負以寬民力。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to comfort the displaced, and remit arrears to ease the people's strength."
translations.idiomatic: It is time to comfort displaced people and remit tax arrears to ease the burden on the people."

sentences.zh: 明年，三殿災，原吉復申前請，亟命所司行之。

translations.literal: The next year the Three Halls burned; Yuanji again pressed his former request, and the Emperor urgently ordered the authorities to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when fire destroyed the Three Halls, Yuanji renewed his earlier request, and the Emperor urgently ordered the authorities to implement it.

sentences.zh: 初以殿災詔求直言，群臣多言都北京非便。

translations.literal: At first, because of the hall fire, an edict sought frank speech; many ministers said making Beijing the capital was not advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: When the hall fire prompted an edict seeking frank counsel, many ministers argued that establishing the capital at Beijing was unwise.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，殺主事蕭儀，曰：「方遷都時，與大臣密議，久而後定，非輕舉也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and killed Director Xiao Yi, saying, "When the capital was moved, I secretly deliberated with ministers; only after long discussion was it settled—not a light undertaking."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and executed Director Xiao Yi, saying, "When the capital was moved, I deliberated in secret with my ministers for a long time before deciding—it was no hasty act."

sentences.zh: 言者因劾大臣。

translations.literal: The memorialists thereupon impeached the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The memorialists thereupon impeached the senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝命跪午門外質辨。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered them to kneel outside the Meridian Gate and dispute the charges.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the ministers to kneel outside the Meridian Gate and answer the charges.

sentences.zh: 大臣爭詈言者，原吉獨奏曰：「彼應詔無罪。

translations.literal: The great ministers all quarreled with the memorialists; Yuanji alone memorialized, saying, "They responded to the edict and are without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The senior ministers quarreled with the memorialists; Yuanji alone memorialized, saying, "They were responding to the edict and are not guilty.

sentences.zh: 臣等備員大臣，不能協贊大計，罪在臣等。」

translations.literal: We who fill posts as great ministers could not jointly assist the great plan—the guilt lies with us."
translations.idiomatic: We who serve as senior ministers failed to assist the great plan adequately—the fault lies with us."

sentences.zh: 帝意解，兩宥之。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind eased and he pardoned both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's anger eased and he pardoned both sides.

sentences.zh: 或尤原吉背初議。

translations.literal: Some blamed Yuanji for betraying his earlier view.
translations.idiomatic: Some blamed Yuanji for abandoning his earlier position.

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾輩歷事久，言雖失，幸上憐之。

translations.literal: He said, "We have served long; though our words erred, fortunately the sovereign pities us.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "We have served for many years; though our counsel was mistaken, fortunately the sovereign is merciful.

sentences.zh: 若言官得罪，所損不細矣。」

translations.literal: If censorial officials are punished, the loss is no small matter."
translations.idiomatic: If censorial officials are punished, the damage will be no small matter."

sentences.zh: 眾始嘆服。

translations.literal: Only then did all sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did everyone admire his judgment.

sentences.zh: 原吉雖居戶部，國家大事輒令詳議。

translations.literal: Though Yuanji held the Revenue post, on great affairs of state he was always ordered to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Although Yuanji headed the Ministry of Revenue, he was always consulted on major affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 帝每禦便殿闕門，召語移時，左右莫得聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor would often hold court at the side hall by the palace gate, summon him to talk for a long while, and those at his side could not hear.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often received him at the side hall by the palace gate and talked with him at length, out of earshot of attendants.

sentences.zh: 退則恂恂若無預者。

translations.literal: On retiring he was respectful, as if he had taken no part.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving he was deferential, as though he had played no part in affairs.

sentences.zh: 交阯平，帝問：「遷官與賞孰便？」

translations.literal: When Jiaozhi was pacified, the Emperor asked, "Which is more convenient—promoting officials or giving rewards?"
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaozhi was pacified, the Emperor asked, "Which is preferable—promoting officials or granting rewards?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「賞費於一時，有限；

translations.literal: He replied, "Rewards cost at one time and are limited;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Rewards are a one-time expense and are limited;

sentences.zh: 遷官為後日費，無窮也。」

translations.literal: promoting officials is expense for later days, without end."
translations.idiomatic: promoting officials creates ongoing expense without end."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 西域法王來朝，帝欲郊勞，原吉不可。

translations.literal: When the Dharma King of the Western Regions came to court, the Emperor wished to greet him with suburban rites; Yuanji disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dharma King of the Western Regions came to court, the Emperor wished to greet him with suburban rites; Yuanji objected.

sentences.zh: 及法王入，原吉見，不拜。

translations.literal: When the Dharma King entered, Yuanji saw him but did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dharma King entered, Yuanji saw him but did not bow.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「卿欲效韓愈耶？」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "Do you wish to imitate Han Yu?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed and said, "Do you wish to imitate Han Yu?"

sentences.zh: 山東唐賽兒反，事平，俘脅從者三千余人至。

translations.literal: In Shandong Tang Sai'er rebelled; when the affair was settled, more than three thousand coerced followers taken captive were brought in.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Sai'er rebelled in Shandong and the uprising was suppressed, more than three thousand coerced followers were brought in as captives.

sentences.zh: 原吉請於帝，悉原之。

translations.literal: Yuanji requested of the Emperor that all be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji asked the Emperor to pardon them all.

sentences.zh: 谷王橞叛，帝疑長沙有通謀者。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Gu rebelled, the Emperor suspected that at Changsha there were conspirators in communication.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Gu rebelled, the Emperor suspected conspirators at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 原吉以百口保之，乃得寢。

translations.literal: Yuanji guaranteed them with a hundred mouths, and the matter was then laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji vouched for them with his own life and those of his family, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十九年冬，帝將大舉征沙漠。

translations.literal: In the winter of the nineteenth year the Emperor was about to launch a great campaign into the desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the nineteenth year the Emperor planned a major campaign into the desert.

sentences.zh: 命原吉與禮部尚書呂震、兵部尚書方賓、工部尚書吳中等議，皆言兵不當出。

translations.literal: He ordered Yuanji, together with Ministers of Rites Lü Zhen, War Fang Bin, and Works Wu Zhong and others, to deliberate; all said troops should not be sent out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yuanji, together with Ministers Lü Zhen of Rites, Fang Bin of War, and Wu Zhong of Works, to deliberate; all agreed that troops should not be sent.

sentences.zh: 未奏，會帝召賓，賓力言軍興費乏，帝不懌。

translations.literal: Before they could memorialize, the Emperor happened to summon Bin; Bin strongly stated that raising troops would exhaust funds, and the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could submit a memorial, the Emperor summoned Fang Bin, who strongly argued that mobilization would exhaust funds; the Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 召原吉問邊儲多寡，對曰：「比年師出無功，軍馬儲蓄十喪八九，災眚叠作，內外俱疲。

translations.literal: He summoned Yuanji and asked how much was stored on the frontier. Yuanji replied, "In recent years campaigns have gone out without success; of military stores nine-tenths or eight-tenths are lost. Disasters have piled up one upon another, and within and without all are weary.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Yuanji and asked about frontier stores. Yuanji replied, "In recent years campaigns have achieved nothing; military stores have been depleted by eight or nine tenths. Disasters have struck repeatedly, and the empire is exhausted within and without.

sentences.zh: 況聖躬少安，尚須調護，乞遣將往征，勿勞車駕。」

translations.literal: Moreover Your Sacred Person has only lately been at ease and still needs care; I beg that generals be sent on campaign and the imperial carriage not be troubled."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty has only recently recovered and still needs care; I beg that generals be sent on campaign rather than troubling the imperial person."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，立命原吉出理開平糧儲。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and immediately ordered Yuanji to go out and manage grain stores at Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and immediately ordered Yuanji to go manage grain stores at Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 而吳中入對如賓言，帝益怒。

translations.literal: When Wu Zhong entered audience and spoke as Bin had, the Emperor grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zhong appeared in audience and spoke as Fang Bin had, the Emperor grew even angrier.

sentences.zh: 召原吉系之內官監，並系大理丞鄒師顏，以嘗署戶部也。

translations.literal: He summoned Yuanji back and imprisoned him in the Inner Palace Directorate, and also imprisoned Assistant Minister of Justice Zou Shiyan, because he had once acted for the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Yuanji and imprisoned him in the Inner Palace Directorate, and also imprisoned Assistant Minister of Justice Zou Shiyan, who had once acted for the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 賓懼自殺。

translations.literal: Bin, in fear, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Bin, in fear, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 遂並籍原吉家，自賜鈔外，惟布衣瓦器。

translations.literal: They then inventoried Yuanji's household; apart from bestowed paper money there were only plain cloth and earthenware.
translations.idiomatic: They then inventoried Yuanji's household; apart from paper money bestowed by the Emperor, they found only plain cloth and earthenware vessels.

sentences.zh: 明年北征，以糧盡引還。

translations.literal: The next year on the northern campaign, when grain was exhausted they turned back.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign the following year, the army turned back when supplies ran out.

sentences.zh: 已，復連歲出塞，皆不見敵。

translations.literal: Afterward, for successive years they went beyond the passes, yet never saw the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Emperor campaigned beyond the passes year after year without ever encountering the enemy.

sentences.zh: 還至榆木川，帝不豫，顧左右曰：「夏原吉愛我。」

translations.literal: Returning to Yumu River, the Emperor was unwell and turned to those at his side, saying, "Xia Yuanji loves me."
translations.idiomatic: On the return to Yumu River the Emperor fell ill and said to those beside him, "Xia Yuanji loves me."

sentences.zh: 崩聞至之三日，太子走系所，呼原吉，哭而告之。

translations.literal: Three days after news of the death arrived, the Heir Apparent ran to the prison, called Yuanji, and weeping told him.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after news of the death arrived, the Crown Prince ran to the prison, called for Yuanji, and weeping told him the news.

sentences.zh: 原吉伏地哭，不能起。

translations.literal: Yuanji lay on the ground weeping and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji lay on the ground weeping and could not rise.

sentences.zh: 太子令出獄，與議喪禮，復問赦詔所宜。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent ordered him released from prison to deliberate on funeral rites, and again asked what was fitting for the amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince ordered him released to deliberate on funeral rites and asked what should be included in the amnesty edict.

sentences.zh: 對以振饑、省賦役、罷西洋取寶船及雲南、交阯采辦諸道金銀課。

translations.literal: He replied with relief for famine, reduction of taxes and corvée, abolition of treasure ships to the Western Ocean, and ending procurement offices in Yunnan, Jiaozhi, and other routes for gold and silver levies.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed famine relief, reduction of taxes and corvée, abolition of treasure fleets to the Western Ocean, and ending procurement of gold and silver in Yunnan, Jiaozhi, and other regions.

sentences.zh: 悉從之。

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: All were adopted.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，復其官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor ascended the throne, Yuanji's office was restored.

sentences.zh: 方原吉在獄，有母喪，至是乞歸終制。

translations.literal: While Yuanji was in prison his mother died; now he begged to return and complete the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuanji was in prison his mother had died; he now asked to return home and complete the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿老臣，當與朕共濟艱難。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "You are an old minister and should with me cross hardship together.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You are a veteran minister and should weather hardship together with me.

sentences.zh: 卿有喪，朕獨無喪乎？」

translations.literal: You have mourning—do I alone have none?"
translations.idiomatic: You are in mourning—am I not in mourning as well?"

sentences.zh: 厚賜之，令家人護喪，馳傳歸葬，有司治喪事。

translations.literal: He richly rewarded him, ordered his family to escort the coffin, sent post-horses for swift return and burial, and had the authorities manage funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He richly rewarded him, ordered his family to escort the coffin home on post horses for burial, and had the authorities manage the funeral.

sentences.zh: 原吉不敢復言。

translations.literal: Yuanji did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji did not dare raise the matter again.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子少傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 呂震以太子少師班原吉上，帝命鴻臚引震列其下。

translations.literal: Lü Zhen, as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, ranked above Yuanji; the Emperor ordered the Court of State Ceremonial to lead Zhen to stand below him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen, as Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince, ranked above Yuanji; the Emperor ordered the Court of State Ceremonial to place Lü Zhen below him in rank.

sentences.zh: 進少保，兼太子少傅、尚書如故，食三祿。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Junior Guardian, concurrently Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Minister as before, with triple stipends.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Guardian, retaining his posts as Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and Minister of Revenue, with triple stipends.

sentences.zh: 原吉固辭，乃聽辭太子少傅祿。

translations.literal: Yuanji firmly declined; only then was he permitted to decline the Junior Tutor's stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji firmly declined, and the Emperor allowed him to forgo the Crown Prince's tutor stipend.

sentences.zh: 賜「繩愆糾繆」銀章，建第於兩京。

translations.literal: He was given a silver seal inscribed "Correcting faults and remedying errors" and residences were built for him in both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: He received a silver seal inscribed "Correcting faults and remedying errors," and residences were built for him in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 已而仁宗崩，太子至自南京。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Renzong died, and the Heir Apparent arrived from Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Renzong died, and the Crown Prince came up from Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 原吉奉遺詔迎於盧溝橋。

translations.literal: Yuanji, following the testamentary edict, welcomed him at the Lugou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Following the testamentary edict, Xia Yuanji welcomed him at the Lugou Bridge.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，以舊輔益親重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, as an old assistant he was all the more trusted and honored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuanzong Emperor came to the throne, he treated this veteran counselor with even greater intimacy and respect.

sentences.zh: 明年，漢王高煦反，亦以「靖難」為辭，移檄罪狀諸大臣，以原吉為首。

translations.literal: The next year the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, rebelled, likewise taking "Pacifying Difficulties" as his plea; he circulated a proclamation listing the crimes of the great ministers, with Yuanji named first.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Prince of Han, Zhu Gaoxu, rebelled, likewise invoking the "Pacification of Difficulties"; he circulated a proclamation denouncing the senior ministers, with Xia Yuanji listed first.

sentences.zh: 帝夜召諸臣議。

translations.literal: At night the Emperor summoned the ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned his ministers for a night council.

sentences.zh: 楊榮首勸帝親征。

translations.literal: Yang Rong was the first to urge the Emperor to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong was the first to urge the Emperor to take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 帝難之。

translations.literal: The Emperor found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hesitated.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「獨不見李景隆已事耶？

translations.literal: Yuanji said, "Have you alone not seen what became of Li Jinglong?
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji said, "Have you forgotten what became of Li Jinglong?

sentences.zh: 臣昨見所遣將，命下即色變，臨事可知矣。

translations.literal: Yesterday I saw the generals you sent out; the moment the order was given their faces changed—how they will act in battle can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I saw the generals you dispatched; the moment they received orders their faces changed—you can guess how they will perform in battle.

sentences.zh: 且兵貴神速，卷甲趨之，所謂先人有奪人之心也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in warfare speed is prized; roll up armor and hurry there—this is what is called seizing the enemy's heart by acting first.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, war favors speed; march at once in full armor—that is how you seize the initiative.

sentences.zh: 榮策善。」

translations.literal: Rong's plan is good."
translations.idiomatic: Rong's plan is sound."

sentences.zh: 帝意遂決。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 師還，賚予加等，賜閽者三人。

translations.literal: When the army returned, rewards and gifts were increased by a grade, and three gatekeepers were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, rewards were increased and he was given three gatekeepers.

sentences.zh: 原吉以無功辭。

translations.literal: Yuanji declined on the grounds of having no merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji declined on the grounds that he had done nothing to deserve them.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 三年，從北巡。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he accompanied the northern tour.

sentences.zh: 帝取原吉橐糗嘗之，笑曰：「何惡也？」

translations.literal: The Emperor took the dried grain from Yuanji's pouch and tasted it, laughing, "How foul!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took the dried grain from Xia Yuanji's pouch and tasted it, laughing, "How wretched this is!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「軍中猶有餒者。」

translations.literal: He replied, "In the army there are still men who go hungry."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "There are still hungry men in the army."

sentences.zh: 帝命賜以大官之饌，且犒將士。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered that he be given the Grand Steward's fare and that the generals and troops be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered court delicacies bestowed on him and rewards given to the officers and troops.

sentences.zh: 從閱武兔兒山，帝怒諸將慢，褫其衣。

translations.literal: He followed the review of troops at Tuer Mountain; the Emperor was angry that the generals were slack and stripped off their garments.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the troop review at Tuer Mountain; the Emperor, angered by the generals' slackness, ordered their garments stripped off.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「將帥，國爪牙，奈何凍而斃之？」

translations.literal: Yuanji said, "Generals are the state's claws and teeth—how can you freeze them to death?"
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji said, "Generals are the claws and teeth of the state—how can you let them freeze to death?"

sentences.zh: 反覆力諫。

translations.literal: He remonstrated repeatedly with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated again and again with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「為卿釋之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "For your sake I release them."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "For your sake I will release them."

sentences.zh: 再與蹇義同賜銀印，文曰：「含弘貞靖。」

translations.literal: He was again given a silver seal together with Jian Yi, inscribed "Broad, forbearing, upright, and tranquil."
translations.idiomatic: He and Jian Yi were again given silver seals inscribed "Broad, forbearing, upright, and tranquil."

sentences.zh: 帝雅善繪事，嘗親畫《壽星圖》以賜。

translations.literal: The Emperor was skilled in painting and once personally painted the "Star of Longevity" to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was skilled at painting and once personally painted the Star of Longevity to bestow on him.

sentences.zh: 其他圖畫、服食、器用、銀幣、玩好之賜，無虛日。

translations.literal: Other gifts of paintings, food and drink, utensils, silver coins, and curios—there was no day without them.
translations.idiomatic: Other gifts of paintings, food, utensils, silver, and curios came almost every day.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，兩朝實錄成，復賜金幣、鞍馬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, when the Veritable Records of the two reigns were complete, he was again given gold coins and saddles and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, when the Veritable Records of the two reigns were completed, he was again given gold, coins, saddles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 旦入謝，歸而卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the morning he entered to give thanks; returning home he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: That morning he went in to give thanks; returning home he died, at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚忠靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Zhongjing (Loyal and Tranquil).

sentences.zh: 敕戶部復其家，世世無所與。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Revenue Ministry to restore his household, exempt from levies for generations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to restore his household to tax exemption for generations.

sentences.zh: 原吉有雅景，人莫能測其際。

translations.literal: Yuanji had refined sensibility; no one could fathom its depths.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji had refined sensibilities that others could not fully fathom.

sentences.zh: 同列有善，即采納之。

translations.literal: If colleagues had something good, he at once adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever colleagues had a good idea, he adopted it at once.

sentences.zh: 或有小過，必為之掩覆。

translations.literal: If they had small faults, he always covered them over.
translations.idiomatic: If they had minor faults, he always covered for them.

sentences.zh: 吏汙所服金織賜衣。

translations.literal: A clerk soiled the gold-brocade robe he was wearing, bestowed by the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk soiled the gold-brocade robe the Emperor had bestowed on him.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「勿怖，汙可浣也。」

translations.literal: Yuanji said, "Do not fear; stains can be washed."
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji said, "Do not be afraid; stains can be washed out."

sentences.zh: 又有汙精微文書者，吏叩頭請死。

translations.literal: Again someone soiled a delicate document; the clerk kowtowed and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion a clerk soiled an important document and kowtowed, begging to die.

sentences.zh: 原吉不問，自入朝引咎，帝命易之。

translations.literal: Yuanji did not inquire; he himself entered court and took the blame, and the Emperor ordered it replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji did not question the clerk; he went to court himself to accept blame, and the Emperor ordered the document replaced.

sentences.zh: 呂震嘗傾原吉。

translations.literal: Lü Zhen once tried to bring Xia Yuanji down.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen once tried to undermine Xia Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 震為子乞官，原吉以震在「靖難」時有守城功，為之請。

translations.literal: When Zhen begged an office for his son, Yuanji, because Zhen had merit in defending the city during "Pacifying Difficulties," pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Zhen asked an office for his son, Xia Yuanji pleaded on his behalf because Lü Zhen had defended the city during the "Pacification of Difficulties".

sentences.zh: 平江伯陳瑄初亦惡原吉，原吉顧時時稱瑄才。

translations.literal: The Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Xuan, at first also disliked Yuanji, yet Yuanji would often praise Xuan's talent.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Xuan, had also disliked Xia Yuanji at first, yet Xia Yuanji often praised Chen Xuan's ability.

sentences.zh: 或問原吉：「量可學乎？」

translations.literal: Someone asked Yuanji, "Can forbearance be learned?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Xia Yuanji, "Can forbearance be learned?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾幼時，有犯未嘗不怒。

translations.literal: He said, "In my youth, when offended I never failed to grow angry.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "In my youth, whenever I was offended I grew angry.

sentences.zh: 始忍於色，中忍於心，久則無可忍矣。」

translations.literal: At first I bore it in my face, then in my heart; after long practice there was nothing I could not bear."
translations.idiomatic: At first I bore it in my expression, then in my heart; in time there was nothing I could not bear."

sentences.zh: 嘗夜閱爰書，撫案而嘆，筆欲下輒止。

translations.literal: Once at night he reviewed legal cases, stroked the desk and sighed, and when the brush was about to descend he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Once at night, reviewing legal cases, he stroked the desk and sighed, and whenever his brush was about to sign a death warrant he stopped.

sentences.zh: 妻問之。

translations.literal: His wife asked him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife asked why.

sentences.zh: 曰：「此歲終大辟奏也。」

translations.literal: He said, "This is the year-end memorial for capital punishment."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "This is the year-end report recommending executions."

sentences.zh: 與同列飲他所，夜歸值雪，過禁門，有欲不下者，原吉曰：「君子不以冥冥墮行。」

translations.literal: Once drinking at a colleague's house, returning at night in snow and passing the forbidden gate, some wished not to dismount; Yuanji said, "A gentleman does not let his conduct fall in the dark."
translations.idiomatic: Once, after drinking at a colleague's home, he returned at night through snow; passing the forbidden gate, some companions wished not to dismount. Xia Yuanji said, "A gentleman does not let his conduct lapse in the dark."

sentences.zh: 其慎如此。

translations.literal: Such was his caution.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his care in conduct.

sentences.zh: 原吉與義皆起家太祖時。

translations.literal: Xia Yuanji and Jian Yi both began their careers under Ming Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji and Jian Yi both began their careers under Taizu.

sentences.zh: 義秉銓政，原吉筦度支，皆二十七年，名位先於三楊。

translations.literal: Yi held the power of selection, Yuanji managed revenue—all for twenty-seven years, their fame and rank preceding the Three Yangs.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi held authority over appointments, Xia Yuanji managed state finances—each for twenty-seven years, and both ranked ahead of the Three Yangs in seniority.

sentences.zh: 仁、宣之世，外兼臺省，內參館閣，與三楊同心輔政。

translations.literal: During the reigns of Renzong and Xuanzong, they held censorial and provincial posts outside the court and served in the Hanlin within it, working with the Three Yangs to assist the government.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Renzong and Xuanzong emperors they held censorial posts abroad and served in the Hanlin at court, working in concert with the Three Yangs to govern.

sentences.zh: 義善謀，榮善斷，而原吉與士奇尤持大體，有古大臣風烈。

translations.literal: Jian Yi was skilled in planning and Yang Rong in deciding, while Xia Yuanji and Yang Shiqi especially upheld the larger principles, with the bearing of great ministers of old.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi excelled at planning, Yang Rong at decision, while Xia Yuanji and Yang Shiqi especially upheld the larger pattern, with the bearing of great ministers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 子瑄，以蔭為尚寶司丞。

translations.literal: His son Xuan, by hereditary privilege, became Director of the Imperial Seals Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan entered office through hereditary privilege as a director in the Imperial Seals Office.

sentences.zh: 喜談兵。

translations.literal: He delighted in discussing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in discussing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 景泰時，數上章言兵事，有沮者，不獲用。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai era he repeatedly memorialized on military affairs; some obstructed him and his proposals were not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign he repeatedly memorialized on military affairs; opponents blocked him and his proposals were not adopted.

sentences.zh: 終南京太常少卿。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 俞士吉，字用貞，象山人。建文中，為兗州訓導。上書言時政，擢御史。出按鳳陽、徽州及湖廣，能辨釋冤獄。成祖即位，進僉都御史。奉詔以水利書賜原吉，因留督浙西農政。湖州逋糧至六十萬石，同事者欲減其數以聞。士吉曰：「欺君病民，吾不為也。」具以實奏，悉得免。尋為都御史陳瑛所劾，與大理少卿袁復同繋獄。復死獄中，士吉謫為事官，治水蘇、松。既而復職，還上《聖孝瑞應頌》。帝曰：「爾為大臣，不言民間利病，乃獻諛耶！」擲還之。宣德初，仕至南京刑部侍郎，致仕。

translations.literal: Yu Shiji, style Yongzhen, was from Xiangshan. During Jianwen he served as training instructor at Yanzhou. He submitted a letter discussing current policy and was promoted to censor. Sent out to inspect Fengyang, Huizhou, and Huguang, he was able to distinguish and release wrongful imprisonments. When Chengzu came to the throne, he was advanced to Assistant Censor-in-Chief. Under imperial order, he took books on water management and bestowed them on Yuanji, and therefore remained to supervise agricultural administration in western Zhejiang. Huzhou owed as much as six hundred thousand shi of grain; his colleagues wanted to reduce the number in reporting it. Shiji said, "To deceive the ruler and harm the people is something I will not do." He fully memorialized the truth, and all were exempted. Soon he was impeached by Chen Ying, Censor-in-Chief, and was imprisoned together with Yuan Fu, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review. Fu died in prison, and Shiji was demoted to managing official and put to work on water control in Suzhou and Songjiang. Later he was restored to office, and on returning submitted the Shengxiao ruiying song. The emperor said, "You are a great minister, yet instead of speaking of the people's benefits and harms, you present flattery?" He threw it back to him. At the beginning of Xuande, Shiji served up to Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiji, style Yongzhen, came from Xiangshan. During Jianwen he was training instructor at Yanzhou. After submitting a memorial on current policy, he was promoted to censor. Sent to inspect Fengyang, Huizhou, and Huguang, he distinguished and released wrongfully imprisoned men. When Chengzu took the throne, Yu was advanced to Assistant Censor-in-Chief. By imperial order he carried books on water management to Yuanji, and he stayed on to supervise agricultural administration in western Zhejiang. Huzhou owed as much as six hundred thousand shi of grain, and his colleagues wanted to report a reduced figure. Shiji said, "To deceive the ruler and harm the people is something I will not do." He reported the facts in full, and all the arrears were remitted. Soon afterward he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying and imprisoned together with Yuan Fu, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review. Yuan Fu died in prison, and Shiji was demoted to managing official and assigned to water control in Suzhou and Songjiang. Later he was restored to office. On his return he submitted the Shengxiao ruiying song. The emperor said, "You are a great minister, yet instead of speaking of the people's benefits and harms, you offer flattery?" and threw it back to him. Early in Xuande, Shiji reached the post of Vice Minister in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and retired.

sentences.zh: 李文郁，襄陽人。

translations.literal: Li Wenyu was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenyu was a native of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，以戶部侍郎副原吉治水有勞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, as Vice Minister of Revenue he assisted Yuanji in water control and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongle reign, as Vice Minister of Revenue he assisted Xia Yuanji in water-control work with distinction.

sentences.zh: 後坐事謫遼東二十年。

translations.literal: Later, implicated in an affair, he was banished to Liaodong for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was implicated in an offense and banished to Liaodong for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，召還，為南京通政參議，致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne he was recalled, made Participating Secretary of the Nanjing Court of Transmission, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor ascended the throne he was recalled, appointed participating secretary of the Nanjing Court of Transmission, and retired.

sentences.zh: 鄒師顏，宣都人。
