translations.literal: Zou Shiyan was a man of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Shiyan came from Yidu.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，為江西參政，坐事免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he was Administrative Commissioner of Jiangxi and was dismissed because of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongle reign he served as administrative commissioner of Jiangxi and was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋以薦擢御史，有直聲。

translations.literal: Soon on recommendation he was promoted to censor and had a reputation for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to censor on recommendation and gained a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 遷大理丞，署戶部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and acted for the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and acted for the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 與原吉同下獄。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned together with Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned together with Xia Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，釋為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne he was released and made Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne he was released and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 省墓歸，還至通州，卒，貧不能歸葬。

translations.literal: Returning from tending his family's graves, he reached Tongzhou and died, too poor to return home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back from visiting his family's graves he reached Tongzhou and died, too poor to transport his body home for burial.

sentences.zh: 尚書呂震聞於朝，宣宗命驛舟送之。

translations.literal: Minister Lü Zhen reported it at court; Emperor Xuanzong ordered a post boat to convey the body.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lü Zhen reported it at court; the Xuanzong Emperor ordered a courier boat to convey the body home.

sentences.zh: 詔京官卒者，皆給驛，著為令。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that when capital officials died, post service should be granted—all established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict decreed that when capital officials died, courier transport should be provided—a rule thereafter fixed in law.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《書》曰「敷求哲人，俾輔於爾後嗣」。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: The Documents says, "Broadly seek the wise to assist your later successors."
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist writes: The Book of Documents says, "Seek widely for the wise to assist your successors."

sentences.zh: 蹇義、夏原吉自筮仕之初，即以誠篤幹濟受知太祖，至成祖，益任以繁劇。

translations.literal: Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji from the beginning of their service were known to Taizu for sincere capability and practical achievement; under Chengzu they were all the more entrusted with heavy duties.
translations.idiomatic: From the start of their careers Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji won Taizu's trust through sincerity and practical ability; under the Chengzu Emperor they were entrusted with ever heavier duties.

sentences.zh: 而二人實能通達政體，諳練章程，稱股肱之任。

translations.literal: The two in truth could penetrate the structure of government and were versed in regulations—worthy of the role of arms and legs.
translations.idiomatic: In truth both understood how government worked and were versed in regulations—true pillars of the state.

sentences.zh: 仁、宣繼體，委寄優隆，同德協心，匡翼令主。

translations.literal: Renzong and Xuanzong succeeded in turn; trust placed in them was generous and high; of one virtue and one mind they aided and supported their excellent sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Renzong and Xuanzong emperors they were entrusted with exceptional favor, working in concert to support their excellent sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 用使吏治修明，民風和樂，成績懋著，蔚為宗臣。

translations.literal: Through them official governance was clarified, the people's customs harmonious and joyful, achievements splendidly shown—they stood as great ministers of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Through them official governance was clarified and the people lived in harmony; their achievements were outstanding, and they stood among the dynasty's greatest ministers.

sentences.zh: 樹人之效，遠矣哉。

translations.literal: The effect of cultivating men—how far-reaching!
translations.idiomatic: How far-reaching is the effect of nurturing worthy men!
